chunks: what the Shaykh — may God strengthen him — informed me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from his father, from al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad, from Hariz, from someone who informed him, from Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him), who said:
'Al-wadiy does not break wudu; it is merely like mucus and saliva.'

key_terms.الْوَدْيُ: al-wadiy — thick white post-urination discharge; distinct from mani (semen) and madhy (pre-seminal fluid); ritually pure (tahir)
key_terms.بِمَنْزِلَةِ: in the legal status/rank of; used by the Imams to establish legal analogies (qiyas) in fiqh
key_terms.يَنْقُضُ: breaks/nullifies wudu; the standard legal term for a hadath-causing event

ai.seo_question: Does al-wadiy (post-urination discharge) break wudu according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) issues a clear jurisprudential ruling that al-wadiy — a thick whitish fluid that sometimes exits after urination — does not nullify wudu, classifying it alongside mucus and saliva as a bodily secretion that is ritually pure. This hadith is foundational in Shia fiqh for the tripartite distinction among post-urethral fluids: mani (semen, which requires ghusl), madhy (pre-seminal fluid, ruling disputed), and wadiy (ritually pure, no action required).
word_analysis: in the legal status/rank of; like
